approach: Physically based wet ground (Lagarde 2013 "Water drop 3", Lekner and Dorf 1988). Outside puddles, a drained film (a few tenths of a mm) is thinner than the ground's relief, so the ground only darkens and gets a broad lobe at the relief's roughness. It has no mirror term and no SSR. Darkening per channel follows Lekner-Dorf, A' = A(1-r_e)(1-r_i)/(1-r_i A), with r_e 0.066 and r_i 0.475 taken from Fresnel at n 1.333, applied to the soaked share of the face (porous soil all of it, dense ground 0.75, grass beads 0.15). The lobe uses water's Fresnel at relief roughness (asphalt 0.65, bare 0.8, grass 0.95, replacing the old film's 0.12). Its sky is the SH sky light around the reflected direction pulled toward the normal by roughness squared. Puddles are a separate level water layer (F0 0.02, roughness 0.05 forward and 0.02 in the trace, rain rings), darkened below by kWetPuddleDark 0.55, which is Lekner-Dorf at albedo 0.2. With wetWeather on, the SSR trace returns at once for pixels with no puddle and otherwise weights by the pixel's puddle share at water's roughness and cone. In wetPuddle (shared by both passes), saturated bare ground ponds like a road once the puddles are full: max(road, level) in the threshold, because saturated trodden soil soaks up only a few mm/h, less than heavy rain. This change gives the night square enough mirrors to read wet. Objects keep their old wet maths exactly. There are no C++ engine changes.

The sun-glint test now counts 3 sun lobes (wet face, puddle, object) and checks that relief roughness sits above the sun floor, since the kWetSunGround* constants were removed. New test "Wet weather ground: only standing water mirrors; the wet face darkens and glints broadly" checks four things. First, r_e and r_i integrated from Fresnel against the constants. Second, the Lekner-Dorf ratio against kWetPuddleDark. Third, the roughness order. Fourth, a C++ mirror of wetLobe for an eye at 1.75 m and a lamp 5 m up and 12 m away: the asphalt glint peaks below 5% of a puddle's and is more than 10x wider. It also checks the trace's early return and puddle-only weight.
weak_points:
1. Night readability is the main risk. With the sheen gone, the night square reads wet through darker ground and puddle mirrors. A puddle that mirrors only the near-black night sky or the fog horizon has little contrast, so seam_b at thumbnail size looks more dark and damp than pouring. The near-black overcast night sky is outside this change.
2. The saturation-ponding rule (bare ground uses the road threshold at full puddle level) makes the seam_day square's puddles noticeably larger. If the owner finds it too much, reverting max(road, level) to road undoes it alone.
3. Lekner-Dorf darkens roads and gravel more than the old 0.35 x porosity did, so the night square is darker overall. This was not checked against photos.
4. A soft broad glint stays near close lamps and the fire by design.
5. The wet face's sky reflection uses an SH irradiance prefilter, which may faintly lift far roads in daylight.
6. Puddle mirrors keep the trace's existing half-resolution banding. Straight vertical lines inside puddles are mirrored building edges, not seams.
7. Not measured: cost (the trace now skips non-puddle ground; the forward pass adds one SH lookup), motion, and the fallback before the ground field is built.
8. The night refl-view numbers include the fog veil that the debug view keeps.
Probe numbers over the ground band: reflection-view pixels above luma 0.15 went from 62% to 17% at night and from 90% to 22% by day. The mean forward lamp glint went from 0.025 to 0.010.

approach: Puddles are placed by the terrain's shape, and only puddles reflect. A basin term from the 12.5 m height map (the hollow against neighbours 1 cell away plus a quarter of the hollow 2.5 cells away on the diagonals) lifts the puddle field by up to 0.1 in hollows; a crest can take away at most 0.2 of that. Slope raises the threshold (0.5 per unit of slope above 0.08), and puddles fade out between 14 % and 25 % slope. The outlines come from the old three noise octaves on a warped position, with each octave rotated off the world axes, so no water line runs along a grid line. Puddles have a wider, darker damp rim and murky water: under a puddle the ground's texture fades 60 % toward the ground-field colour. Outside puddles the screen-space reflection weight is 0 when wetWeather is on, and the trace skips the march there. The forward ground film is 0.25 of its old share at roughness 0.65. Sealed ground (asphalt, gravel) now darkens like soil instead of shining.

unit_tests:
PoseidonTests.exe "[wet],[ssr],[Shaders],[TerrainHorizon],[remaster]" run from D:\ passed: 957261 assertions in 300 test cases, and glslang compiles every program. All three changed files are clang-format clean. Round 3's no-seam tests are kept; one string changed to match the new threshold line. Three new tests:
- Shape placement, using C++ mirrors on synthetic 12.5 m grids. Water share: bowl 0.307, level 0.138, crest 0.101, 3 % slope 0.118, 8 % 0.092, 15 % 0.065, 25 % 0.
- Water-line direction: 9.5 % of water lines run within 5 degrees of the world axes, against 12.7 % for the old noise on the axes (an even spread would be 11.1 %).
- Only puddles mirror: string checks on the trace's weight and early out, the ground film, the soak floor, the damp rim and the murky water.
weak_points:
- **Night views:** they read darker and less obviously rainy than round 3. With matte ground, rain shows as darker colour, a few puddles and the streaks in the air. Puddles at night mirror a dark sky unless a lit wall, the lamp or the fire lines up behind them.
- **Town square:** probes show it sits on a 3 to 6 % convex rise with a crest about 0.15 m high, so shape placement leaves its foreground sparse. If the owner wants more water there, the knobs are kPuddleSlopeFree and kPuddleCrest.
- **rain_day:** the meadow slopes about 10 to 14 %, so it now holds only small puddles in its left hollow. The jeep puddle and its straight edge are gone because no puddle is placed there any more; the underlying cause is not fixed. That cause is in the trace's fallback when a ray passes behind a vehicle: it uses the hull's dark underside, which draws a mirror-image edge wherever a puddle runs under a vehicle. That fallback is unchanged; the murky water only keeps the puddle itself visible.
- **No road ruts:** neither pass knows which way a road runs, so ruts were not attempted.
- **Height map resolution:** at 12.5 m per texel it picks the areas that collect water; each puddle's outline still comes from noise.
- **Probe values are approximate:** they pass through the post chain. Puddle share in the final frames and the frame cost were not measured.

approach: Smallest safe change, keeping round 3's structure. Outside the puddles I only turned the reflections down, through constants and two masks. In the forward pass (wetSurface), the ground's film is multiplied by kWetGroundFilm 0.1 and held at least kWetGroundFilmRough 0.55 rough, so lamp, window and fire streaks become a dim, broad smudge. In the SSR trace, the non-puddle sheen weight under the wet weather is multiplied by kSsrWetSheen 0.08, and mix(sheen, 1.0, puddle) keeps puddles as full mirrors. Puddle terms are untouched. A probe showed that without the sheen, night puddles that mirror only the overcast sky come out about as bright as the wet ground. Round 3's puddles had only read as dark holes in the bright sheen. A darker puddle bed (0.55 to 0.3) moved them by just 2 to 3 levels, so I dropped it. Instead I added a little more water (kPuddleRoad 0.61 to 0.58, kPuddleGround 0.67 to 0.63, mirrored in B6's kSsrPuddle* so the cross-pass pin holds). I also widened and darkened the damp margin (kPuddleDamp 0.06 to 0.1, kWetDampDark 0.9 to 0.85) for some patchy darkening that has no edge. I tuned through 5 shader-override variants plus a puddle-mask probe, then baked the result into the source, rebuilt and shot the finals.

weak_points: The night views read as rainy only faintly. The probe showed the puddles are still there, but those that mirror only the overcast night sky are about as bright as the wet ground, and a darker puddle bed barely helped. Pure tuning cannot fix that; it needs a brighter, cloud-lit night sky in the puddle mirror, puddles placed where they catch lights, or rain rings that sparkle. In town_night_rain no puddle lies between the fire or the lamp and the eye, so neither throws a reflection at all. That meets the target but the owner may miss it. More puddles also changes B6's legacy path (rain with wetWeather off), because its thresholds are pinned to the forward pass's. Round 3's thin bright rim at some puddle edges remains. Day views barely change. Shot-to-shot smoke timing differs. Motion and cost were not measured; the change adds no texture reads.

approach: Audit first, then cut. A probe override keyed on the forced wetness knob (wetness = 1 - p/1000, read in both the forward pass and the SSR trace) let one game shoot every probe, each turning off one term: film lamp streaks, film sun/moon glint, SSR on non-puddle ground, the surface lane's ground specular, the forward sky env, all puddle terms, all non-puddle terms together, plus a puddle mask, camBloom=0, fogLights=0 and the SSR reflection-only view. The world wetness in these views is 1.00, so forcing it changes nothing. Result: the film's lamp streaks carry 34-36% (town_night_rain) and 54-61% (seam_b) of the light on non-puddle ground in the two regions. Every other ground term is within noise (a few percent). SSR on non-puddle ground is small but mirrors the houses on the road. Bloom and fog glow cannot be read as ground terms: the camera's metering confounds them. The cut, all in shaders: (1) outside puddles the ground's lamp lobe takes the ground glint roughness and share (0.6 rough, 0.3 of the film), so it is a dim broad patch, not a streak; (2) with the wet weather on, the SSR weight is the puddle alone; (3) the forward sky env on the ground is the puddle's alone; (4) the film darkens the ground instead (kWetGroundFilmDark 0.25); (5) roads and bare ground hold slightly more water (kPuddleMore 0.04, grass unchanged), inside the shared seamless puddle field.

approach: Art direction around one rule: only standing water mirrors. In the reflections' trace, with the wet weather on, any texel with less standing water than kSsrMirrorMin (0.004) now traces nothing, and the mirror weight outside the water is 0. Inside a puddle the water stays a sharp level mirror right to its edge: roughness 0.02, cone 0.003, normal straight up, with the puddle's share fading it at the rim. In the forward pass, wet ground and roads outside the water darken by 0.2 x (1 - grass) on top of the porosity darkening, gain a little saturation (0.12), and keep only 0.3 of the film at roughness 0.6 or more. Their lamp and fire glints are computed as if the eye were at least about 31 degrees above the ground, so a light leaves a dim, rounder pool at its foot instead of a column toward the eye. The puddle bed darkens from 0.55 to 0.42 so the mirror stands out. The puddle threshold stays at bare ground's value until the grass share passes 0.6, so the mixed town square holds more water while meadows do not change.
owner_line: Wet ground is darker, with only a soft warm pool of light around the fire and lamps and no streaks or sheen; the square has more puddles, and they are now the only things that reflect, as clear mirrors of the lamp, fire, houses and sky.

New test "Wet weather: only the puddles mirror...": the trace's early-out, zero ground weight and sharp mirror to the edge; the new forward constants and where they are used; a C++ copy of wetLobe showing the raised-view glint is under 0.35x the grazing lobe at its peak and along the tongue toward the eye, at least as wide across, and no closer to the eye; and the puddle threshold rising smoothly with no step.
weak_points: 1. The rainy read now depends on where the noise puts puddles. town_night_rain and seam_day have plenty, but the foregrounds of seam_b and seam_d happen to be dry, so at thumbnail size those two read more as a damp night than a downpour. I left kPuddleGround alone because a C++ constant pins it. 2. Puddles right at the camera's feet are dark: water reflects only about 2% when you look down at it. Only mid-distance puddles carry bright images. 3. The raised-view glint is an art-directed cheat, so the pool at a light's foot does not slide with the eye. Motion and TAA were not checked. 4. The rain rings only move the light glints drawn on the puddle (the forward pass); the mirrored image (the reflection trace) has only a small noise ripple, so reflected images look calm. 5. Puddles sit in new places compared with round 3 and the rework, and the share was not measured with a probe tint. 6. Performance cost was not measured; the trace should be cheaper because it now skips most wet ground. 7. Other agents share the scratchpad and overwrote one of my helper scripts there, so I moved all my working files to GR/tmp/look/puddle/5/work. Notes are in D:/Arma_CWA_worktrees/graphics-remaster/tmp/look/puddle/5/NOTES.txt. Only this copy's games were stopped; it had none running at the end.

approach: Only puddles reflect, and the puddles get better. In the trace, with the wet weather on, the non-puddle wet sheen is multiplied by kSsrDampWeight = 0, so the ground outside puddles reflects nothing. In the forward pass the ground film is never smoother than 0.55 and only 0.35 of it glints, which leaves a dim broad pool of light near a lamp and no streaks. Bare ground soaks at least 0.6 and ground darkening goes from 0.35 to 0.5, so rain shows as darker, deeper colour. Puddles stay crisp mirrors with Schlick water Fresnel and cone 0.008. Rain rings plus a gentle moving chop (puddleRings, now in the shared puddles piece) disturb both the trace's mirror and the forward lamp and sun glints. Both fade out with the pixel's footprint, so far puddles stay calm. The water body is darker (0.55 to 0.4) and there is a darker wet rim (0.9 to 0.6 over a shorter margin). Bare ground and roads hold more water (thresholds 0.67 to 0.6 and 0.61 to 0.56; grass unchanged). Where the trace misses (a ray behind a vehicle or level out of frame), a puddle falls back to a dim guess of the sky.
